reviews.head: 2d7ac626
reviews.note: I found two blocking defects: the scheduled pull silently drops logs if the backlog exceeds the 1,000-log page limit, and the analytics query silently underreports the 7-day totals if there are more than 10,000 calls.

findings.text: If a pull hits `MAX_PAGES` before reaching the last mark (e.g. after a spike of >1,000 calls), `fetchNewLogs` returns the newest 1,000 logs and `pullGateway` unconditionally advances the mark to the newest of them, permanently dropping all older unread logs.

`windowSql` selects individual rows with a hard limit of 10,000; if there are more than 10,000 calls in the 7-day window, older calls are silently omitted from the query result, causing the Models page and CLI to underreport the window's true total cost, tokens, and calls.

If the `METRICS` binding is somehow missing or misconfigured, `writeLog` returns false and writes nothing, but the mark is still advanced, meaning those logs will be skipped forever once the binding is fixed.

reviews.head: 04cafbf6
reviews.note: The earlier blocking findings are resolved (a capped pull records its gap, totals are summed in SQL without a row limit, and writing oldest-first prevents advancing the mark on failure), but a new data-loss defect was found where pagination stops prematurely and drops older logs if the API returns invalid logs on a full page.

findings.text: `fetchNewLogs` uses the filtered `found.length < PAGE_SIZE` to stop paging; if the API returns a full page of 50 logs but one fails to parse (e.g., missing ID), `found.length` is less than 50, causing the pull to stop prematurely, return `gap: null`, and silently drop all older valid logs without recording a gap.

reviews.head: de671943
reviews.note: I verified that all earlier blocking findings are resolved (capped pulls correctly record the gap, SQL queries sum totals without row limits, failed writes leave the mark unchanged, and short pages are accurately judged by raw result length), and I found no new correctness, security, or data-loss defects in this change.

verdicts.head: 04cafbf6
verdicts.note: Fixed: fetchNewLogs judges a short page by the raw result length, not the parsed logs; test in test/gateway.test.ts fails without it.

reviews.head: 097f3af5
reviews.note: I checked the HEAD and trailing-slash routing, the 404 handling under /api and for unknown pages, and the Origin check on POST /login; the new 404-versus-redirect split on /p/<name> lets anyone signed out confirm which projects are registered, including anonymised and private ones.

findings.text: A signed-out visitor to /p/<name> gets a 303 when the name (current or former) is registered and a 404 when it is not, so anyone can confirm private or anonymised project names by guessing them; before this change every such path redirected alike, and the task aims to stop anonymised projects being re-identified.
API_PATHS leaves out "runners", which api() serves, so a signed-out GET /api/runners answers 404 instead of 401; it is still refused, but the list has already drifted from api().

The task also asks for a per-client rate limit on POST /login and for commit hashes to be left out of anonymised showcase projects; this change does neither and no commit claims to, so both remain to do.
The Origin test for POST /login only tries a foreign origin; it does not check that a matching origin or a missing Origin header still reaches the token check.

reviews.head: aea15054
reviews.note: Round 1's blocking finding is fixed (every signed-out /p/ path now redirects to sign-in alike), as are its runners and Origin-test follow-ups; the HEAD, trailing-slash, unknown-path 404 and login Origin routing is correct, and only the rate limit and commit-hash work remain as follow-ups.

findings.text: The task also asks for a per-client rate limit on POST /login and for commit hashes to be left out of anonymised showcase projects; neither is done yet (no commit claims them), so both are still to do.

API_PATHS is a hand-kept copy of the top-level names api() serves; a route added to api() later and not here will answer a signed-out caller 404 instead of 401, so a test should tie the two lists together.

reviews.head: c5089f44
reviews.note: The change correctly restricts the runner to its configured jobs locally, but breaks the server's `unoffered` check for plain builds because `src/dispatch/rules.ts` was not updated to enforce `"build"` in `offer.jobs`.

findings.text: The runner relies on local filtering to skip plain builds because the server's `assign()` does not check if `offer.jobs` includes `"build"`. This divergence causes `unoffered()` in `src/dispatch/rules.ts` to incorrectly return `null` for a dispatched build when the only live runner is reviews-only, suppressing the warning in `atelier status` while the build hangs indefinitely.

reviews.head: 0adceecd
reviews.note: The earlier finding from round 1 regarding the server's unoffered logic and plain builds is resolved, and the new implementation correctly enforces exact job configurations while preserving backward compatibility.

findings.text: A runner configured with exactly `jobs: ["merge-main-task"]` will be silently denied task merge-main jobs because `needs` evaluates to `["merge-main", null, "merge-main-task", null]`, causing the server to incorrectly demand `"merge-main"` as well.

reviews.head: 20a35a7b
reviews.note: I verified that the earlier blocking finding regarding plain builds is resolved, but found that exact job configuration is broken for task merge-main jobs, preventing a runner from being dedicated to them.

findings.text: A runner configured with exactly `jobs: ["merge-main-task"]` will be silently denied task merge-main jobs because `needs` evaluates to `["merge-main", null, "merge-main-task", null]`, causing the server to incorrectly demand `"merge-main"` as well.

reviews.note: I verified that both earlier blocking findings are resolved: plain builds are now correctly checked against the "build" job server-side to prevent hanging reviews, and task merge-main jobs correctly ask for "merge-main-task" instead of "merge-main" in `missingJob`; no new correctness, security, or data-loss defects were introduced.

verdicts.head: 20a35a7b
verdicts.note: Fixed in 3a1d7a2: missingJob asks merge-main-task in place of merge-main for a task's merge-main, as jobOf names it; the new test in test/plans-state.test.ts fails without the fix.
